Thanks for taking this — I lead integrations at Pinecone Solutions and wanted to open a short intake thread so we can map connector capabilities and any obvious gaps before a pilot. We propose a joint engineering call next week to cover:

Alex — thanks for the clear intake. Looping in Marissa (partnerships), Karthik (runtime/product), and Ben (SRE/infra) so we can prepare a technical brief. A few clarifying requests from our side before the call so we can make the session productive: 

- Can you confirm whether Pinecone's upsert api preserves client-supplied IDs or performs an internal remap? That affects our dedup window and reindex plan.
- In your spec you list payload size limits per vector — what are the exact limits for metadata blob vs vector bytes?
- For S3 cold-tier fallback: do you provide a manifest + pre-signed URL approach or do you require server-side pull from a bucket?
- Do you support streaming per-document acknowledgements, or only bulk success/failure responses?

Action items for us before the call:

Vanessa / Alex — quick notes from the Weaviate side (we're doing integration work with a few customers that mirror the flow you described):

> On Fri, Mar 2, 2028 at 10:01 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> > Can you confirm whether Pinecone's upsert api preserves client-supplied IDs or performs an internal remap?

- Pinecone preserves client IDs by default; they do allow generated IDs as an option but you can opt to control IDs on upsert.

> > payload size limits for metadata blob vs vector bytes?

- Practical limits we've seen in prod: metadata JSON up to ~64KB comfortably; vector binary limited by overall request size (Pinecone example: ~1MB total payload by default). That said, Redwood's runtime may need stricter chunking to honor low-latency SLOs.

> > S3 cold-tier fallback approach

- Most partners implement a manifest + pre-signed object approach. Server-side pull is possible but requires tighter IAM and cross-account roles; manifests are easier operationally.

> > streaming acks vs bulk responses

- Weaviate and Pinecone both primarily give bulk success/failure for batch upserts; streaming per-item acks are rare in managed vector DBs. Consider idempotent write keys and an ingestion checkpoint stream (Kafka or S3 manifests) for reconciliation.

I've attached a quick network_diagram.png showing a common egress pattern and where tracing headers are easiest to pass. Happy to join the intake call Tue 10:00 PT if your teams want our integration engineer present.

—Deepa
